question.text: A conducting circular loop of area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> and resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> is placed perpendicular to a uniform time varying magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mfenced><mi>t</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mi>sin</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>50</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. What is the net charge (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mC</mi></math>) flowing through the loop during <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math> <mrow> <mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>ms</mtext></mrow> </math>?
